ădĭtĭo , ōnis, f. 1. adeo.
I. A going to, approach: quid tibi hanc aditio est? (i. e. aditio ad hanc, the verbal substantive with the case of the verb; “v. Zumpt, § 681),”
why do you approach her?
Plaut. Truc. 2, 7, 62 : “praetoris,” Dig. 39, 1, 1 al. —
II. hereditatis, the entering upon an inheritance (v. 1. adeo, II. A.), Dig. 50, 17, 77 al.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
